title: Cubic-rate irrationality for reciprocal sums
abstract: Every positive strictly increasing zero-indexed integer sequence a with n^3(a_n^2/a_(n+1) - 1 - 3/n) tending to zero has an irrational reciprocal sum. The entry also states the exact integer-tail and number-field steps used to exclude the resulting cubic profile: positive-density exceptions, primitive gcd reduction, square specialisation, scale twelve, forbidden words modulo seven, and regular-rate extraction. The printed one-indexed paper theorem uses its stated finite-prefix argument. The separate bounded-increment Sylvester criterion in the paper is outside this configuration, and the unrestricted Erdős problem #243 remains open. The selected Challenge explicitly retains the strict monotonicity and positivity of a, the HasSum witness for its reciprocal series, and the n³-scaled rate limit. It does not silently infer that rate from the weaker condition a_(n+1)/a_n² → 1.
